content_metadata.description: In this video, Jo shares her personal experiences addressing airport security as an amputee. She discusses both the procedures and the challenges involved, offering advice and observations based on her journey before and after acquiring a prosthetic leg.

qAndA.question: What is the name of the YouTube channel?

qAndA.answer: Airport security thought she had a weird substance on her hand, but it turned out to be legal medication.
qAndA.question: Why was Jo detained by airport security on one occasion?

qAndA.answer: Jo does not take her prosthetic leg off. The security agents fully search her body and also test the prosthetic leg for chemicals using a dry pad.
qAndA.question: What does Jo do with her prosthetic leg when going through airport security?

qAndA.answer: Yes, she recommends requesting a wheelchair if you anticipate having to walk a lot, especially in larger airports.
qAndA.question: Does Jo recommend requesting a wheelchair at the airport?

qAndA.answer: Inform the security personnel about your situation and explain that you cannot remove your shoes for medical reasons. They will then follow alternative security procedures.
qAndA.question: What does Jo recommend doing if you're an amputee and cannot remove your shoes for medical reasons?

youtube_description:
What is it like going through TSA - airport security - as an amputee, with a prosthetic leg? I definitely had a lot of questions going into it. This has been my personal experience!

TSA Information: https://www.tsa.gov/travel/special-procedures

#amputee #amputation #tsa

MY STORY //

Fourteen years of pain and failed ankle surgeries brought me to 2018, when I made the difficult decision to become a twenty-seven-year-old below-the-knee elective amputee. This channel is to document my journey of amputation surgery, recovery, and reclaiming my life.

I use the Ossur ProFlex XC Torsion foot/ankle with a direct socket with passive vaccum suction.
